description: exact? failing proves "no ONE lemma closes this", not absence — on a composite goal it makes a free step look like the blocker

---

A failing `exact?` measures absence only when the goal is **atomic**. On a goal
that is a composite of library facts it measures the absence of a *one-lemma*
proof, which is much weaker — and the error always points the same way: the step
looks HARDER than it is.

I ran `exact?` on an iso `T_{k'} ×_T T_{k'} ≅` (a base change), it failed, and I
published in a docstring *and* a commit message that this was THE open link of the
step. It decomposed into two mathlib lemmas: `Over.forget` preserves pullbacks
(`PreservesPullback.iso`, by synthesis), then `pullbackRightPullbackFstIso`. Two
lines.

**Why:** the cost is not the wasted probe, it is that a gap named as *the blocker*
gets a lane assigned to it while the real residue stays unlooked-at. Mine was two
levels further on, so I would have handed a peer the wrong target. Same session, a
peer made the inverse error — inferring a binder on *my* step from an iff about
*their* theorem. Both are one measurement read as a statement about a neighbouring
object; see [[price-the-consumer-carrier]] and [[goals-measure-difficulty-not-ingredients]].

objects, decompose it once by hand and probe each piece. If the object is built by a
chain of pullbacks, slices or base changes, that chain IS the decomposition. Reserve
the unqualified "absent" for goals with nothing to decompose — a class at a specific
object, a named property of a named map — which is where the existing absence lore

---
name: scratch-dirs-not-gitignored
description: Per-project Scratch*/ dirs are NOT ignored in this workspace; another lane's sweep commits your sorried probe files
metadata:

---

In the Archon Horizon workspace, per-project scratch directories
(`MainProjects/<project>/Scratch2/`, `ScratchWR/`, …) are **untracked but not
ignored**. The workspace `.gitignore` rule is `/*probe*.lean` — anchored to the
workspace root and matched on the substring `probe`, so it covers a probe file
dropped at the root and nothing under a member project.

Measured 2026-07-30: `git check-ignore -v` on my scratch file returned empty; 28 of
my probe files reached HEAD via another lane's integrate sweep. Three contained
deliberate `sorry` and several contained deliberately *failing* probes
(non-vacuity controls that must not close). Nothing is rooted in a module, so no
build sees them and no sorry-census counts them — a later reader finds sorried Lean
with no way to tell it was a control. Independently measured by two other lanes,
including 11 such files in the sibling project, 7 with `sorry`.

**Why:** "stage explicit files, never `add -A`" protects your own commit, not your
files from someone else's sweep. Related to [[uncommitted-work-reaches-head-via-other-lanes]]
and the inverse direction of [[commit-stat-names-files-you-never-touched]].

**How to apply:** assume anything you write under a member project can reach HEAD
without your staging it. Delete the scratch directory before session end (a
dedicated commit with `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1`, staged list verified to
contain only those paths). Do not claim a scratch dir is "gitignored" in a docstring
or inbox item without running `check-ignore` — several lanes including me asserted it
without checking, and one lane "verified" it by testing files they had just named
`probe_*.lean`.
